title: Police officer who saved woman's life cleared by SIU
article: The province's Special Investigations Unit has cleared a Toronto Police officer in the March 28 fatal shooting of a 37-year-old man at a North York apartment building.
Police were called to 3460 Keele St. for a domestic dispute that morning at 8:46 a.m.

The SIU said Cristian Iordache, a visitor from Windsor, hit his wife in an apartment, chased after her as she ran into the common hallway and followed her back into the apartment where he continued the attack.

The first responding officer arrived at 8:49 a.m. and met witnesses in the building lobby. A woman told the officer that she thought Iordache was going to kill his wife and may be armed with a knife. The officer noticed fresh blood on the walls and door frame outside the apartment and heard a woman crying. He entered the apartment and found Iordache holding a long two-pronged barbecue fork. His wife was bleeding from the chest.

The officer drew his gun and ordered Iordache to drop the knife. Iordache was shot in the chest at 8:51 a.m. when he started to stab his wife in the neck. He was pronounced dead in hospital an hour later. His wife was treated in hospital for puncture wounds to the neck, a deep cut to the hand and bruising.

The SIU, a civilian agency that investigators whenever there is a serious injury or death involving police, assigned eight investigators to the case and designated one subject officer and eight witness officers.
